KP125M page confirms: Energy monitoring YES, Matter YES, Hub NO (Wi-Fi direct), 15A/1800W, UL certified, scheduling YES, away mode YES, Alexa/Google/Apple Home/ SmartThings/Bixby, indoor only, compact, 2-year warranty.

Emporia Smart Plug help page (help.emporiaenergy.com) confirms: Energy monitoring YES (Emporia app, Vue integration), Hub NO (Wi-Fi direct), 15A peak / 10A continuous, indoor ONLY (explicitly says 'not rated for outdoor use'), scheduling YES, away mode YES (app-based), Alexa/Google Home, compact, 1-year warranty. The outdoor row in the article correctly cites this source. ASIN B0CLVV7X7Y not independently verifiable.

DOE standby power page (energy.gov/cmei/femp/measuring-standby-power) confirms definition: 'Standby power consumption is defined as the lowest power consumption while plugged into the mains power supply.'
DOE Better Buildings page is still live and supports advanced power strip recommendation.

Body claims of '2 W in standby' threshold and '1-5 W standby' range are expert guidance claims — no direct DOE document quotes an exact 2W threshold. The 2W figure is a common industry heuristic (ENERGY STAR, various efficiency programs). Should be softened to 'devices drawing more than 1-2 W in standby are strong candidates — a common industry threshold' and cited to general practice, not a specific DOE anchor.

Safety section correctly states 15A / 1,800W limit — matches all four manufacturer spec sheets. Space heater 1,500W = 12.5A calculation confirmed (1,500/120 = 12.5A). The safety guidance is accurate and well-sourced to manufacturer ratings.
Table footnote about 120V only is accurate — all four product pages specify 100-125V / 120V AC input voltage.

ASINs in product-box shortcodes at bottom may cause Amazon affiliate linking issues if SKU name changes — the KP125MP2 ASIN (B0BYGRLRS1) should work if Amazon's listing uses that bundle identifier, but the model name displayed to users must be 'KP125M' not 'KP125MP2'.
